definitions.gloss: low price, bargain price, low value
definitions.explanation: A price that is low or cheap. Frequently used in financial and market contexts to describe stocks, commodities, or goods at a low price point. The opposite is {高値|たかね} (high price).

examples.english: I was able to buy it at a low price.

examples.japanese: {株価|かぶか}が{年初来|ねんしょらい}{安値|やすね}を{更新|こうしん}した。
examples.english: The stock price hit a new year-to-date low.

examples.japanese: {円|えん}{安|やす}の{影響|えいきょう}で{輸入品|ゆにゅうひん}が{安値|やすね}では{手|て}に{入|はい}らなくなった。
examples.english: Due to the weak yen, imported goods are no longer available at low prices.

notes:
USAGE:
Especially common in financial reporting and market analysis. Often appears with superlative-like expressions: {最安値|さいやすね} (lowest price), {年初来|ねんしょらい}{安値|やすね} (year-to-date low), {史上|しじょう}{最安値|さいやすね} (all-time low).

SIMILAR WORDS:
The opposite is {高値|たかね} (high price). For everyday shopping, {安|やす}い (cheap) is more common; {安値|やすね} has a more financial or market-oriented tone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {安値|やすね}で{買|か}う: to buy at a low price
- {安値|やすね}を{更新|こうしん}する: to hit a new low
- {最安値|さいやすね}: lowest price, all-time low
- {年初来|ねんしょらい}{安値|やすね}: year-to-date low
- {安値|やすね}{圏|けん}: low price range
